title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Artificial intelligence dominated tech news this Wednesday, with Positron securing $230 million in Series B funding to challenge Nvidia and Intel entering the GPU market. Developer tools are integrating advanced AI, notably through Xcode 26.3’s agentic coding capabilities. Lotus Health’s AI doctor platform and Fitbit’s Luffu AI platform represent AI’s expansion into specialized healthcare applications.  India’s Varaha received $20 million for carbon removal efforts, demonstrating growing investment in environmental AI.  Regulatory action included a Supreme Court warning to WhatsApp regarding user privacy and a police search of X’s Paris office involving Elon Musk. Y Combinator announced seed funding options via stablecoins.

Business news saw the S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures decline due to AI-driven sell-offs, while the Dow Jones futures rose. Walmart surpassed a trillion-dollar market cap, and Santander finalized a $12.2 billion acquisition of Webster. Shell divested a stake in its Orca Project, and Equinor reported lower earnings despite record production. NXP’s outlook was boosted by demand for “physical AI.”

Globally, the conflict in Ukraine continued, with condemnation of Russian attacks.  Israeli strikes in Gaza resulted in casualties, and a Greek coast guard boat collision tragically killed 15 migrants.  An Iranian drone was shot down by the U.S. military, and Saif al-Islam Gaddafi was reportedly killed in Libya.  The House shelved a contempt vote regarding the Epstein investigation, and Spain announced a ban on social media for minors.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
The Overnight Market Brief – Pre-Market Edition for February 3, 2026, provides a market overview following yesterday’s risk-on performance on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 up 0.54% and the Nasdaq 100 rising 0.73%. Key macro indicators include a 10-Year Treasury yield at 4.287%, a declining US Dollar Index at 97.41, and a significant surge in gold to $4939.3, reflecting a flight to safety.

Overnight, Asian markets experienced positive momentum, driven by a US-India trade deal and strong Hong Kong retail sales, with the Nikkei 225 up 3.92% and Greater China indices rising. European markets adopted a cautious approach ahead of the upcoming ECB decision. US futures are currently higher, with S&P 500 futures up 0.28% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.54%, indicating a rotation into growth-oriented tech.

Investors are closely monitoring the ECB meeting, the potential unwinding of the yen carry trade, and the implications of the US-India trade deal. With a light economic calendar, market direction is expected to be influenced by these thematic developments and technical positioning, suggesting a path of higher resistance.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap for February 3, 2026, reveals a rotation out of growth stocks and into defensive sectors following a mixed trading day. The S&P 500 dipped 0.84% to 6917.81, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.55% to 25338.62 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average decreased 0.34% to 49240.99. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a cautious rebalancing rather than a panicked sell-off.

Sector performance highlighted a shift towards defensive plays, with Utilities (XLU) rising 1.50% and Technology (XLK) declining 2.23%. This divergence indicates investor preference for safety and value over high-growth tech. The US Dollar Index decreased 0.28% to 97.22, halting a recent rally. Crude Oil prices increased 2.89% to $63.94.

Tech giants, including Nvidia (-2.84%), Microsoft (-2.85%), Apple (-0.19%), Alphabet (-1.15%), Amazon (-1.76%), and Meta (-2.09%), experienced significant declines, driven by digesting recent earnings and concerns about AI competition. Palantir (PLTR) saw a notable surge after-hours.

Analysts believe the market is reassessing growth prospects and positioning for a slower growth environment. Investors will be closely watching for Federal Reserve guidance and corporate earnings to provide clarity on monetary policy and influence equity valuations.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary: Tensions escalated in the Arabian Sea as the U.S. shot down an Iranian drone approaching the USS Abraham Lincoln. Simultaneously, thousands of previously sealed Epstein documents were released, sparking outrage and accusations of a lack of transparency. The House Oversight Committee reached an agreement for former President Clinton and Secretary of State Clinton to testify. In Ukraine, a record-breaking missile and drone barrage caused widespread power outages, raising concerns about intensified conflict. Spain announced a ban on social media access for minors, aiming to protect children from online risks. Tragically, fourteen migrants died after a vessel collision in the Aegean Sea. Finally, a trade deal between India and the U.S. saw the U.S. slashing tariffs on Indian goods in exchange for India halting Russian oil imports, marking a significant strategic realignment.
